Q1: Should this fix also cover the group 1 failure, `test_four_failed_fetches_report_transport_5xx_and_keep_retry_policy`, which the issue's affected-files list leaves out?
Choices:
A) Yes. Apply the same monotonic-clock change to `review_head_checkout_now_ms` in `scripts/review_autofix_step_checkout_pr_head_branch.sh`: read `/proc/uptime`, and fall back to the current `date` path if that fails. Also clamp negative results in `review_head_checkout_elapsed_ms` to `0` so `fetch_ms` and `switch_ms` keep the `<n|na>` contract, where `na` means only "never started". Add contract tests that lock the clamp behaviour. (RECOMMENDED)
B) No. Limit this issue to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py` as filed. Group 1 is handled separately, by re-running the job or by a separate triage issue.
C) Only loosen the test. Change `tests/test_review_checkout_head_diagnostics.py:208` to accept `na` and leave the script alone.
**Note:** C weakens the telemetry contract instead of fixing the root cause. Picking it also leaves the clock bug in the script.
Q2: How should this fix handle open PR #9246, which already touches the same heartbeat clock in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`?
Choices:
A) Go ahead regardless. Make the smallest self-contained edit here, and let normal merge-conflict handling sort out any overlap with #9246, #9274 or #9277 if they land first. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Treat #9246 as the fix for group 3. If Q1 is A, this issue covers only the checkout-head script; if Q1 is B, it closes as a duplicate.
C) Wait until #9246 merges, then re-check whether any part of this failure is still left.
